content.text: When Stripe restricts your access in Zimbabwe, Nigeria, Ghana, or other regions, [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/build-crypto-payments-tanzanian-online-sellers-until-you|Do Not]]ing-crypto-store-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-workers-crypto-payment-webhooks-what-actually-how-4|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]]-pages-works-how-7|building]] a crypto store on Cloudflare Pages is the solution. Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages offer free hosting for digital creators, but payment infrastructure like NOWPayments enables seamless crypto transactions without relying on Stripe or other restricted payment platforms. With COREMERCH's stacks, you can deploy a fully functional digital store in 4-6 hours (Stack 01) or 48 hours (Stack 02), depending on your requirements. This guide will walk you through a step-by-step deployment process for a crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, empowering you to sell digital products without any platform restrictions or fees.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

COREMERCH's infrastructure is designed to combat the limitations imposed by payment platforms like Stripe. It provides a sovereign solution that allows digital creators to own their infrastructure, eliminate subscription fees, and maintain control over their data. By leveraging Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, or NOWPayments, you can host and process payments on your own terms, unhindered by geographical restrictions or platform policies.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, you'll need a few essential tools. These include a Cloudflare account, a GitHub account (if opting for GitHub Pages), and the NOWPayments integration. Additionally, you'll need to create a new Cloudflare Pages site and a GitHub Pages site (if using GitHub). If you're planning to deploy Stack 02, you'll require the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) for a faster deployment experience and end-to-end testing. After acquiring these resources, you're ready to proceed with the setup process.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to configure NOWPayments and create a new Cloudflare Worker. This worker will handle payment processing, product delivery, and secure storage of customer data. You can use the NOWPayments API to link your crypto wallet and set up automatic payment processing. Additionally, you'll need to configure your Cloudflare Pages site to point to your worker, ensuring seamless payment and delivery functionality. This setup will enable you to process transactions instantly and securely.
The entire sovereign stack — hosting, payments, delivery, order storage — has zero monthly cost after the one-time deployment.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you can proceed to deploy your crypto store on Cloudflare Pages. This involves uploading your site code to Cloudflare Pages and configuring your worker to receive incoming payments. When a customer makes a purchase, your worker will automatically process the transaction and deliver the product. You'll receive the payment in your crypto wallet, and the customer will receive their product instantly. This end-to-end process ensures a seamless and secure transaction experience for both parties.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your crypto store is up and running, you can scale your infrastructure to accommodate increased traffic and sales. This involves upgrading your Cloudflare Pages site to a paid plan, adding more workers to handle increased payment processing, and configuring additional security measures to prevent DDoS attacks. COREMERCH's Edge Commerce Stack ($197) offers end-to-end testing and support to ensure a smooth scaling experience. By scaling your infrastructure, you can ensure that your crypto store remains responsive and reliable, even during periods of high demand.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link.
Test a real mainnet transaction before you promote — finding a configuration error with your own crypto costs less than finding it with a buyer's.

If you're looking for a more comprehensive solution, consider investing in the Edge Commerce Stack ($197), which deploys Stack 02 in 48 hours and offers end-to-end testing. For more information on COREMERCH's products, visit their website at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. This guide has provided a step-by-step deployment process for a crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, empowering you to sell digital products without any platform restrictions or fees.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, follow these steps: Create a new Cloudflare account and set up a Cloudflare Pages site. Acquire the necessary resources, including a NOWPayments account and a Cloudflare Worker. Configure your NOWPayments account to link your crypto wallet and set up automatic payment processing. Deploy your site code to Cloudflare Pages and configure your worker to receive incoming payments. Test your payment and delivery pipeline to ensure a seamless transaction experience. Finally, scale your infrastructure as needed to accommodate increased traffic and sales.

Yes, you can use GitHub Pages instead of Cloudflare Pages. However, keep in mind that GitHub Pages has some limitations compared to Cloudflare Pages, including slower performance and fewer scalability options. Nonetheless, GitHub Pages remains a viable option for hosting digital stores.
